title: Beyond-Birthday XRKA Round Bounds for Iterated Even-Mansour
summary: A generic attack requires a master key longer than n bits for beyond-birthday related-key security; the schedule-dependent minimum round count for Iterated Even-Mansour remains conjectural.

formal_statement.body: For a $2n$-bit master key, determine whether XRKA security beyond the birthday bound requires at least 6 rounds with a linear key schedule and at least 2 rounds with a nonlinear key schedule.

scope.domain: XRKA security of iterated Even-Mansour block ciphers with linear or nonlinear key schedules.
parameters: n: bit-length variable used to define the 2n-bit master-key size
key-schedule type: linear or nonlinear, determining which conjectured round threshold applies
round count: proposed minimum needed for security beyond the birthday bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute the necessity of at least six linear-schedule rounds and at least two nonlinear-schedule rounds for beyond-birthday XRKA security with a 2n-bit master key.

citations.label: On the Provable Security of the Iterated Even-Mansour Cipher Against Related-Key and Chosen-Key Attacks

progress.summary: The source first notes that a generic attack makes a master key longer than n necessary for beyond-birthday related-key security. It then explicitly conjectures six-round and two-round minima for linear and nonlinear key schedules, respectively, with a 2n-bit master key.
citation_labels: Benoît Cogliati et al., On the Provable Security of the Iterated Even-Mansour Cipher Against Related-Key and Chosen-Key Attacks
